title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
authors: V. Karpukhin, B. Oğuz, S. Min, P. Lewis, L. Wu, S. Edunov, D. Chen, W. Yih
before: Retrieval meant BM25 and other term-matching methods.
problem: Keyword matching misses paraphrase, so the right passage is often invisible to the retriever.
breakthrough: Two BERT encoders trained so that questions and their answering passages land near each other in vector space.
why: It beat BM25 decisively and made dense retrieval the default first stage in RAG.
next: RAG plugged it into a generator; hybrid dense-sparse retrieval followed.
inherits: The dual-encoder retriever at the front of most RAG systems.
